title: Source locality of the universal single-rank predicate
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:T\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $E,F$ be module sheaves on $X$. If every point $t\in T$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ such that $R_1(f,E,F,g\circ\iota_V)$ holds [def-sc-picard-universal-single-rank-match], then $R_1(f,E,F,g)$ holds. No flatness, properness or finite local freeness hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Fix a test h:Tprime->T and tprime in Tprime. Choose V containing h(tprime) with R_1 on V. The inverse-image open Vprime contains tprime, and h restricts to a morphism Vprime->V. Apply R_1 on V to this map and the corresponding point. It supplies an open U in Vprime, a natural number r, and the two rank-r witnesses.

Regard U as an open in Tprime by its image under the open immersion Vprime->Tprime. Open base change identifies the direct image restricted to Vprime with the direct image on the corresponding cartesian square: both have the same sections on each open. Tensor pullback composes up to its canonical adjunction isomorphism. Applying these isomorphisms and restricting to U transports both witnesses to the defining witnesses in Tprime. The point lies in this U. Since h and tprime were arbitrary the condition holds; empty tests have no points.
